scope: Two final model-passed cases in audit-revision-batch4.json, assessed against all retained source abstracts, licensed full-text context, actual public payloads, and current bundled companion cases. No repository edits or real-model calls.
method: Read complete entries/private keys/reviewers and inspect the public payload and rendered clinical prompt separately.
Check source entailment, population, newer/older guidance, essential care, contraindications, timing and pair independence.
Verify canonical entry hashes, all source hashes and all literal cited quotations.
Independently retrieve article XML for the sole retained full-text source and verify source identity, reuse license and every retained section.

external_full_text_verification.comparison: Each retained section body, after whitespace normalization, is contained in the retrieved article XML body.

findings.finding: The patient is asymptomatic, 47, previously unscreened, without relevant personal/family/hereditary risk factors or a life-limiting illness. This matches the USPSTF 45-49 average-risk screening population, AGA average-risk definition, and ACS initiation framework. The history does not call for symptomatic diagnostic evaluation instead of screening.

USPSTF, AGA and ACS substantively support initiation at 45. AGA directly lists all five named screening choices and selection according to availability and preference. ACS explicitly requires timely colonoscopy after any positive noncolonoscopy screen. A includes this essential completion step, without inventing a test interval or claiming all choices have identical performance.

Read all eight retained abstracts. The 2019 BMJ guideline uses a risk-based approach but expressly applies to ages 50-79, outside this 47-year-old case; it does not establish a competing recommendation to defer this patient. The 2020 and 2024 NCCN abstracts describe scope rather than supplying an alternative initiation cutoff. The ACR 2024 update independently supports CT colonography at ages 45-75. The answer is therefore not marked wrong merely for adhering to another applicable supplied framework.

Inspected the complete public payload and rendered prompt. The neutral title/question and presenting history do not state an initiation age, name the intended modality choice, or disclose follow-up colonoscopy. No private rationale, evidence claims, hard-hook text, reasoning divergence, or grading keywords are in the public case.

The final bundled examination case concerns lung-cancer screening under an explicitly named ACS framework, with tobacco pack-years, curative-treatment eligibility, annual low-dose CT and cessation support. This case concerns average-risk colorectal screening initiation, selection among several modalities and colonoscopy after positive screening. Both concern prevention, but their eligibility rules and care pathways are different; this is not only a change of numbers or wording.
All eight sources in this artifact contain retained abstracts only. No licensed full-text excerpts or image assets are present; all abstract hashes were verified.

The adult healthcare worker has a recent deep percutaneous injury from a visibly blood-contaminated hollow-bore needle that was in a vein, with known source HIV and detectable viremia. The retained PHS guideline directly identifies these as higher-inoculum transmission-risk features. Presentation at 90 minutes is within the prompt-treatment window. The source is not undetectable, and the worker is not using PrEP, so those shared-decision exceptions do not displace the main recommendation.

The PHS guideline expressly supports immediate PEP, 28-day duration, a guideline-listed three-drug regimen, adherence counseling and reassessment within 72 hours. The German-Austrian guideline review independently supports early triple-drug PEP and standardized procedures to prevent initiation delay. A follows those actions; B incorrectly makes repeat source viral load and baseline worker testing prerequisites to starting.

The 72-hour claim describes the recommended routine initiation window. The retained PHS text also allows expert consultation for high-risk presentations beyond 72 hours; this case at 90 minutes does not test or exclude that exception. The answer does not choose a specific dose despite the source table requiring adjustments/expert input for organ dysfunction, and the chart records no known renal/hepatic disease or regular interacting medications.

Wound washing is already completed. A resolves the urgent HIV prophylaxis decision and provides counseling and early follow-up. It says not to postpone initiation for test results, not to omit baseline or follow-up testing, HBV/HCV evaluation, or secondary-transmission precautions. The retained PHS context explicitly includes laboratory testing and follow-up in the broader exposure protocol and states HBV/HCV guidance is published separately. A does not claim its short answer is the entire exposure protocol or that follow-up can stop after the 72-hour review.

Inspected the complete public payload and rendered prompt. The title, question, problem list and note provide completed injury care and exposure facts without disclosing PEP initiation, duration, regimen count or review timing. Private key, claims and grading metadata are excluded.

The final occupational practice companion concerns removal/reassignment after confirmed isocyanate-induced occupational asthma despite ventilation/PPE. The present case tests time-sensitive HIV prophylaxis after a blood exposure; source population, hazard, intervention and timing are distinct.

Independently retrieved the supplied Europe PMC XML. Metadata identifies PMID 41569270, PMCID PMC12616222, DOI 10.1017/ice.2025.10254 and the matching PHS guideline title. The article license explicitly links CC BY 4.0 and identifies US-government work. Every one of the 52 retained full-text sections matches normalized XML body text. The retained license URL is accurate and permits unrestricted reuse with attribution.
